intro: Understand why GPU utilization can remain low and how to test safe fixes. This Digital Racer guide focuses on decisions a player can check in ordinary gameplay, not secret unlocks or promises of certain results. The exact conditions depend on mode, device and current update, so begin with the rules and settings that the official game actually exposes. Aim for a repeatable process that improves awareness, safety and consistency instead of copying a single dramatic clip.

sections.heading: Record consistent frame data
paragraphs: Use one map and similar camera conditions across repeated short tests. Compare FPS, frame-time spikes, GPU load and CPU per-core activity. An idle lobby's GPU utilization cannot establish the cause of performance drops in fights.

sections.heading: Understand a saturated CPU thread
paragraphs: An emulator can bottleneck one core while overall CPU use remains moderate. The graphics card then waits for new frames and appears underused. Raising settings can increase GPU load without meaningfully increasing the frame rate.

sections.heading: Check the supported FPS limit
paragraphs: Compare GameLoop's active frame setting with the game's current graphics options. A 60 FPS cap can leave spare GPU capacity on a healthy system. Do not use protected-file edits or unlockers merely to show a higher hardware percentage.

sections.heading: Confirm the correct GPU
paragraphs: Use Windows graphics preferences and the driver panel to assign verified emulator executables to the intended graphics adapter. Restart after changing a preference. Avoid indiscriminate global overrides that could hurt unrelated Windows programs.

sections.heading: Watch RAM and temperatures
paragraphs: Paging, thermal throttling and background software can produce stutters even with low GPU usage. Close unnecessary tasks and monitor a sustained match. Do not disable Windows security or critical system services to chase synthetic performance.

sections.heading: Prioritize frame pacing
paragraphs: Compare sustained lows and input responsiveness, not just average FPS or utilization. Revert changes that cause crashes. A stable supported frame rate can feel better than repeatedly bouncing between fast and slow intervals.

sections.heading: How to test the advice without overreacting
paragraphs: For a reliable comparison, note the present settings and record the symptom before changing anything. Make only one supported adjustment, restart the affected application when appropriate and retest the same situation. Revert changes that worsen stability, security or comfort. A percentage or benchmark without practical improvement is not a good reason to keep a tweak. Use only official game and operating-system controls where possible.
